description.purpose: The tool surface of one assistant as ONE node with ONE contract: `tool_call` in, `tool_result` out -- and, since 1.2.0, a second question it answers about ITSELF: name the tools you use and take their schemas back on `tool_schemas`. Which occupant serves a call is decided inside the hive, on `hop.tool_name`. Because the contract names lanes rather than cells, the whole implementation is one `swap_nodes` away from being something else: N tool cells today, one code-executing cell tomorrow, with no edge of the caller moving. Since 1.3.0 every occupant is REACHABLE: the two that stood here unwired, `mcp` and `vault`, are gone -- a cell type is not a tool, and an occupant nobody can reach teaches nothing (GH #547). Since 1.4.0 the two halves of the build round are named as a pair: `build` and `apply` are `build-draft` and `build-apply`, because one fetches a draft and the other submits it, and a shared prefix makes the pair visible in the graph (GH #554). The tool names the model sees are untouched -- `build_topology` and `apply_manifest` are the contract surface, and a cell name is not a tool name. Since 1.4.1 the `build_topology` schema says what the builder actually does: the credential road rides in the level's own declaration rather than a second one beside it, and a member wish answers with the person and the two devices a member always gets (GH #543). Since 1.4.2 it says they ride in ONE submission: the devices draw into scopes only the person creates, and two submissions handed to a front in the same turn have no order at all (GH #585). Since 1.4.1 the ONE file root that `file` and `edit` share is a LITERAL `params.base_path` rather than a substitution token out of the colony's environment ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138)), so a mutation repoints both halves in one act and two assistants in one colony no longer reach the same directory. What is left in `.env` here is the search endpoint, declared and not required.
description.use_when: One per assistant. Draw ONE edge to the hive path stamping `hop.route = 'tool_call'`, and one back off it on `tool_result` -- the pairing is declared in `params.required_drains` and a mutation that wires only the first is refused. A cell that USES tools draws the second pair as well, `in_schemas` out and `tool_schemas` back, and asks once at start-up with the names its own template declares. `params.ports` is empty: the hive path is the only address, so no caller can grow an edge to a single tool and thereby pin the set.
description.not_in_scope: No per-tool credentials: a cell that needs one binds it itself, late, from the environment. No judgement about which tool to call or whether it should have been called -- that happened upstream, and a hive that re-decided it would be a second brain with no conversation in front of it. No record of WHO asked for which schemas: what a cell uses is declared in that cell's own template, and a subscriber table here would be a second copy of it that drifts on the first rewiring. No memory tool either: a memory is a hive of the MEMBER (ADR-0002 E1) and reaching it is a lane of its own, not an occupant of this one. And no MCP SERVER as an occupant -- an MCP server is something a cell talks to. Since 1.3.0 the `mcp` CELL is not an occupant either, and neither is a `vault` (GH #547): a cell type is not a tool. This hive holds the cells this agent's tool calls REACH. A `vault` answers exactly one sender, its broker, and stands in the broker's own hive beside `invoke` -- which is what `templates/access` already ships. An `mcp` bridges ONE named server and is wired the day somebody names it. Both stood here unwired for four minor versions, and an occupant nobody can reach is a placeholder with documentation attached.
examples: a brain emits a tool_call bundle -> the dispatcher splits it -> one message per call reaches this hive on hop.route == 'tool_call' -> one tool_result comes back per call, whichever tool ran

a cell starts and sends {"tools": ["web_search", "web_fetch"]} on in_schemas -> two declarations come back on tool_schemas, and a name the hive does not have comes back in `unknown` rather than as a silence

adding a tool is a change INSIDE this hive: one occupant directory, two edges in `params.graph`, one row in the `schemas` cell's table -- no change to the caller, which is the property the single contract buys
hop.tool_name == 'web_search' selects the search occupant; the two environment tokens it binds (SEARCH_ENDPOINT, SEARCH_API_KEY) are declared in `requires.env` and carry no value in this tree

SEARCH_ENDPOINT.because: binds `params.endpoint` of the `web_search` occupant, which is written `${SEARCH_ENDPOINT:-http://127.0.0.1:8080/search}`. Declared and NOT required, and both halves are deliberate: the token is declared because a builder should learn this template's environment surface by reading it rather than by watching a tool answer nothing, and it is not required because the value has a default -- an instantiation that only wants the shell and the fetcher must not be refused for a search endpoint it will never call. Unset, the search occupant queries the loopback placeholder and returns whatever that is (nothing, on a machine without a search shim); it is not an error and nothing anywhere says so, which is exactly why the key is written down here

SEARCH_API_KEY.because: binds `params.api_key` of the `web_search` occupant, written `${SEARCH_API_KEY:-}`. Not required, because the cell filters the empty string and queries the endpoint anonymously -- that is the occupant's own declared contract (`contract.settings.api_key`), and requiring the key here would contradict the cell it configures. Set it when the configured endpoint wants a bearer token. It carries no value in this tree and never should: the token is the name of a secret, not the secret

sandbox_union.because: The widest occupant wins on every axis, and on every axis the widest is an occupant that declares no `params.sandbox` at all. Four do: `web_fetch` and `web_search` (egress IS what those two cells do -- `network: "deny"` would turn them off, and a process sandbox has no notion of an allowed host), and `file` and `edit` (they do their own I/O rather than starting a runner, so a process sandbox has nothing to bound here; their fence is `params.base_path`, checked lexically and again after canonicalisation). Any single one of those four therefore sets the whole hive to trust `full`, network `allow`, filesystem `unrestricted`. The five that DO carry a block -- `bash`, `unknown`, `build-draft`, `build-apply` and `schemas`, all of them `trust: restricted`, network `deny`, `filesystem.runtime: true`, the tightest in the library -- tighten nothing about the hive as a WHOLE: a union is not an average, and what they bound is what happens once dispatch has already chosen them. This reads uncomfortable and it is meant to: the radius already exists collectively and was invisible while it was spread over separate `config.json` files. Written down, it is what a replacement is measured against -- a single code-executing cell that needs exactly this is not a widening, and one that needs more is, visibly, in the diff of this file. Until 1.3.0 the sum also counted `mcp` and `vault`, two occupants no edge reached; they left the hive with GH #547, and a union over the occupants that actually answer is the narrower and the honest one.

bash.because: One-shot execution by ruling: no persistent session, no shell state and no working directory carried from one call to the next (a call that needs one writes `cd /x && cmd`). Two calls in flight are two processes that cannot observe each other, so a brain may fan a round out across this occupant. `params.max_concurrency: 4` caps how many run at once -- a queue, not a serialisation: the fifth call waits and still answers on its own `tool_result`.

web_fetch.because: A stateless request/response cell: one GET per call, nothing carried between calls, no cookie jar and no session. `params.max_concurrency: 4` caps the parallel fetches for the endpoint's sake, which delays a call but never reorders or merges one.

web_search.because: A stateless request/response cell against the configured endpoint: one query per call, no cursor and no pagination state to be confused by a second call. `params.max_concurrency: 8`, same reading as above.

unknown.because: It formats a string out of the hop it was handed and emits it. It reads nothing, writes nothing and executes nothing, so there is no state for a concurrent call to reach. Declared explicitly although it is not a tool: #286's hazard is a swap that quietly turns a parallel tool round sequential, and a declaration with a hole cannot catch that -- the occupant nobody declared is the one whose serialisation surprises the caller.

build-draft.because: It reads a hop and a turn and writes a turn: no disk, no network, no state of its own. The correlation of a round runs over `tool_call_id`, which travels in the CONTEXT of that round's own message, so two builds in flight cannot reach each other's. What they DO share is the builder at the OS level -- one baumeister for the whole colony -- and that is a queue there, not a serialisation here: the second round waits for its own answer and still gets it under its own id.

build-apply.because: The same shape: it carries a manifest out and a receipt back, keeping nothing. Two submissions in flight are two manifests the colony rolls off one after the other, in the order they reach the mutation door -- and because a manifest has no rollback, that order is the colony's to decide and never this cell's to assume.

file.because: A stateless request/response cell over the filesystem: one op per call, no handle and no cursor carried between calls, so `params.max_concurrency` is a queue and never a serialisation. Two READS of one file cannot disturb each other; two WRITES of one path race in the filesystem rather than in this cell, and that is the caller's ordering to make -- which is exactly why the neighbour `edit` answers this question the other way.

edit.because: The one `false` in this block, and it is the reason the block exists. An edit is a read-modify-write with no lock and no tempfile+rename (`cell-types.md` § edit: "Concurrent edit on the same file: race condition possible ... The caller topology serializes if needed"). A caller cannot see that hazard from outside, so this occupant serialises instead of asking it to: `params.max_concurrency: 1`, a strict queue. A brain may still fan a round out across the other occupants; the edits of that round run one after another.

schemas.because: It reads a list of names and writes a list of declarations out of a table that is compiled into its own script. No disk, no network, no state, nothing shared -- two start-up questions in flight cannot reach each other, and they are the only kind of message it ever gets.
